definitions.explanation: actively putting ideas, theories, or plans into action; practical application rather than theory

examples.japanese: {理論|りろん}を{実践|じっせん}する。
{計画|けいかく}を{実践|じっせん}に{移|うつ}す。
examples.english: To put a plan into action.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{自分|じぶん}の{信念|しんねん}を{日々|ひび}{実践|じっせん}している。
examples.english: He puts his beliefs into practice every day.

notes:
USAGE:
- {実践|じっせん}する (to practice, to put into action)
- {実践|じっせん}に{移|うつ}す (to put into practice)
- {実践的|じっせんてき} (practical - adjective form)

CONTRAST:
- {理論|りろん} (theory) vs {実践|じっせん} (practice)
- {学|まな}ぶ (to learn) vs {実践|じっせん}する (to practice)

COLLOCATIONS:
- {実践|じっせん}{経験|けいけん} (practical experience)
- {実践|じっせん}{知識|ちしき} (practical knowledge)
- {実践|じっせん}{倫理|りんり} (practical ethics)

RELATED:
- {実行|じっこう} (execution, carrying out)
- {実施|じっし} (implementation)
- {応用|おうよう} (application)
